plan: Second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values and risk-neutral, rational opponents. Truthful bidding is a weakly dominant strategy: overbidding risks negative payoff if you win when the second-highest bid is between your value and your inflated bid; underbidding risks losing when winning would be profitable. With no usable history (single round), and values uniformly 0–49 with $0.1 granularity, maximization of expected profit dictates bidding exactly my value. Therefore, I bid 39.0 to win whenever the second-highest bid is below 39 and pay that second-highest bid, yielding nonnegative surplus.

[This is a 3-bidder independent private values second-price auction. The weakly dominant strategy is to bid your true value: overbidding risks winning and paying above your value; underbidding risks losing profitable wins. With rational opponents likely doing the same, optimal long-run and single-round behavior is truthful bidding. Values are in $0.1 increments, and 27.0 complies. Therefore, bid exactly your value to maximize expected profit and avoid dominated strategies.]

[ This is a standard second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values and rational bidders. The dominant strategy is to bid one’s true value: bidding your value ensures you win exactly when your value exceeds the others’ and you pay the second-highest bid. Shading risks losing profitable wins without reducing the price when you still win. There’s only 1 round, so no dynamic considerations apply. Values are uniform 0–49; our value is 13, which is relatively low, so we likely lose, but truthful bidding maximizes expected profit. Bid in 0.1 increments; 13 is valid. ]
